biological.citation: Unknown et al. 2025 - HNF4α-Mediated LINC02560 Promotes Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma Progression by Targeting the miR-505-5p/PDE4C Axis (PMID: 40427523)
biological.summary: In PTC cell lines (KTC-1, BCPAP), LINC02560 sponges miR-505-5p and relieves its suppression of PDE4C. This activates P-AKT and EMT signaling and promotes proliferation, migration and invasion. HNF4α drives LINC02560 expression, so the HNF4α/LINC02560/miR-505-5p/PDE4C axis acts oncogenically in PTC.

biological.citation: Integrated analysis using methylation and gene expression microarrays reveals PDE4C as a prognostic biomarker in human glioma (PMID: 24842301)
biological.summary: PDE4C promoter is hypermethylated and its expression reduced in high-grade glioma, which correlates with grade progression and poorer survival. Demethylation with 5-Aza-dC upregulated PDE4C in glioma cell lines. PDE4C siRNA reduced WT p53, and in U87 cells PDE4C promoted apoptosis and inhibited migration, suggesting a tumor-suppressor role via the p53 pathway.
biological.sample_size: 124 patient samples (56 low-grade, 63 high-grade glioma, 5 normal brain)

biological.citation: Multiple splice variants of phosphodiesterase PDE4C cloned from human lung and testis (PMID: 9349724)
biological.summary: Cloned multiple human PDE4C splice variants (PDE4C-791, -426, -delta54, -delta109). PDE4C-delta54 and the 426-aa form are enzymatically active, and delta54 is sensitive to PDE4 inhibitors. The delta109 form lacks activity. Isoform expression is tissue-specific: delta54 only in testis, and the 5'-extended 791 form only in lung and G361 melanoma cells.

biological.citation: Purification and physical characterization of cloned human cAMP phosphodiesterases PDE-4D and -4C (PMID: 9515166)
biological.summary: Recombinant human PDE4C (61.4 kDa) was expressed in Sf9 cells and purified about 125-fold. Biophysical analysis showed PDE4C forms are highly asymmetric molecules that can form dimers.

biological.citation: Hypoxia-conditioned BMSC exosomes improve short-term spinal cord injury outcomes via the miR-615-3p/PDE4C-mediated cAMP/PKA pathway (PMID: 41526970)
biological.summary: miR-615-3p in hypoxic BMSC exosomes directly targets and suppresses PDE4C, activating cAMP/PKA signaling. This modulates calcium signaling and reduces mitochondrial calcium overload and ER stress in injured spinal neurons. In a mouse SCI model, exosome treatment downregulated PDE4C and improved functional recovery.

biological.citation: Phosphodiesterase 4 inhibition synergizes with relaxin signaling to promote decidualization of human endometrial stromal cells (PMID: 14715868)
biological.summary: PDE4C and PDE4D gene expression was significantly upregulated during in vitro decidualization of human endometrial stromal cells. PDE4 (rolipram-sensitive) activity is central to cAMP control, and PDE4 inhibition synergizes with relaxin to drive decidualization.
biological.significance: significant upregulation (p-value not specified in abstract)

biological.citation: Differential regulation of human antigen-specific Th1 and Th2 lymphocyte responses by isozyme selective cyclic nucleotide phosphodiesterase inhibitors (PMID: 9223593)
biological.summary: Th1 clones showed reduced PDE4C expression, and lacked PDE4D, compared with Th2 clones. This differential PDE4 isoform expression may explain the greater sensitivity of Th2 cells to rolipram.

biological.citation: Genetic loci for alcohol-related life events and substance-induced affective symptoms: indexing the 'dark side' of addiction (PMID: 30718457)
biological.summary: Whole-genome sequencing association and rare-variant analysis found rare missense and splice-site variants in PDE4C associated with alcohol-related life events. The signal had converging evidence in American Indian and European American cohorts.

biological.citation: Neuroprotective Effects of Qi Jing Wan and Its Active Ingredient Diosgenin Against Cognitive Impairment in Plateau Hypoxia (PMID: 40430556)
biological.summary: In mouse models of plateau hypoxia, transcriptomics indicated that diosgenin protects cognitive function and alleviates hypoxic brain damage by regulating PDE4C expression.

biological.citation: Expression and function of phosphodiesterases (PDEs) in the rat urinary bladder (PMID: 28687079)
biological.summary: PDE4C mRNA was not detected in neonatal or adult rat urinary bladder, although PDE4A, 4B and 4D were expressed. This indicates a restricted tissue distribution for PDE4C.
